errors.remediation: Run `jade init`, or set JADE_CONFIG to a jade.config.yaml.
The server refused the token. Make a new one and store it: `jade secret set <name>`.
This Vault accepts ?token= in URLs. Update Jade Vault to 2.18.3 or later. Only for diagnosis: --accept-legacy.
Base refused the task credential (revoked or expired). The task stops; it is not retried. Start the task again.
Install keyring (`pip install keyring`), or allow a 0600 file with --accept-file-secrets.
Store it with `jade secret set <name>`, or set the environment variable JADE_SECRET_<NAME>.
Check the URL in jade.config.yaml and that the server is running (`jade doctor`).
The server speaks another MCP protocol version. Update the server or the toolkit.
The target answered with an error; the message says which.
The target's version is outside what STACK.md allows. Upgrade the target or the toolkit (`jade doctor`).
The call took longer than its timeout. Pass timeout= / --timeout, or check the target.
The same idempotency key was used with other arguments. Use a new key for a new call.
Allow it in jade.config.yaml under approvals, or confirm interactively.
A deny rule in jade.config.yaml matches. Deny wins; change the rule to allow it.
Destructive or unknown operations need a person to confirm, or --yolo (logged).
Review it, then `jade playbook approve <name>`. Any edit needs a new approval.
Fix jade.config.yaml at the place the message names (`jade config show`).
Fix the playbook at the place the message names (`jade playbook check <name>`).
Fix the site spec at the place the message names (`jade site check`).
The target has no such tool. List them: `jade base tools`.
More than one target has this tool. Name the target.
Check the name; list what exists with the matching `list` command.
Run `python build/build.py` and commit the result.
Run `jade doctor` and fix what it reports, or pass --force to go on anyway.

nav.doc: The top bar: the site's name, links to its pages, a theme switch and, with a backend, Sign in.

links.doc: links [{"label", "href"}] (default: every page with nav = true)

hero.doc: The opening: a big title, a line under it, buttons and an optional image.

subtitle.doc: one or two sentences (default: the site tagline)

features.doc: A grid of features: an icon (emoji or short text), a title and a sentence each.

pricing.doc: Plans. With a backend: the live plans and Subscribe buttons (Stripe Checkout). Without: the plans you list.

auth.doc: Sign in, create an account, reset a password (needs a backend). After signing in, go to `next`.

next.doc: where to go after signing in, e.g. /account

account.doc: The signed-in user's plan, usage, billing and API keys; signed out, a sign-in form (needs a backend).

chat.doc: An AI chat. mode gateway: the backend's models for signed-in users. mode ollama: the visitor pastes an Ollama Cloud key. mode demo: a scripted demo.

tools.doc: give the model the kit's workspace tools (files, shell)

form.doc: A form that saves to a backend collection (waitlists, contact forms, signups). The collection must let anyone create.

fields.doc: field specs "name:type!" (type: text, email, number, url, textarea, checkbox; ! = required) or {"name","label","type","required"}

records.doc: Cards listing records of a public backend collection (products, posts, team, …).

collection.doc: collection name (its list rule must allow the visitor)

title_field.doc: field shown as the card title

image_field.doc: file field shown as the image

sort.doc: sort, e.g. title or -price (-created needs a created field)

faq.doc: Questions and answers that open and close.

cta.doc: A call to action: a heading, a line and a button, on a coloured band.

markdown.doc: Text written in markdown (or a .md file next to jade.toml).

file.doc: a markdown file, relative to jade.toml

gallery.doc: A grid of images with captions.

code.doc: A code block with copy and highlighting.

surface.doc: UI from a Jade surface spec (components, data, actions), e.g. a calculator, a dashboard or a quiz.

spec.doc: a surface spec: {root, components, data} (see the UI/UX catalog)

file.doc: a saved surface spec (YAML or JSON), relative to jade.site.yaml: reuse a design instead of rebuilding it

html.doc: Your own HTML, as it is (an escape hatch).

footer.doc: The bottom of the page: a line of text and links.

templates.chatbot: A chatbot site, with a full-page chat for signed-in users and a floating help widget on every page.
templates.dashboard: An analytics dashboard built from a surface spec (KPIs, charts, a sortable table), with sign-in.
templates.docs: A documentation site from Markdown files (no backend needed).
templates.landing: A one-page product landing site (no backend needed).
templates.portfolio: A personal portfolio with work, a gallery and a contact form.
templates.saas: An AI API business, with pricing, sign-up, an account page with keys and usage, a chat playground and docs.
templates.shop: A small shop: products listed from the backend, accounts, and a support chat widget.
templates.waitlist: A launch page with a waitlist form saved to the backend (anyone can join; only admins can read it).
